Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Maya: giving him space is fine for now, and please don’t try a new training approach without checking with the behavior team. Maya: thanks, all. Tess: Please label the food bins before they go out. We have chicken kibble, salmon kibble, and the sensitive-stomach formula, and two of the bags look almost identical in the storage room.

Andre: I put colored tape on those three bins this morning: blue for chicken, green for salmon, and orange for sensitive stomach. The feeding cards have the same colors now.

Nora: I’ll be at the storage unit around 11:30 on Saturday. If anyone needs to add a supply request, send it by Friday evening so I can check the shelves before the pickup.

Devon: We received two new applications this morning. One is from a family with a fenced yard asking about adult dogs; the other is from an apartment resident interested in a small, calm dog.

Maya: I’ll review both applications after work and check references before suggesting any matches. We don’t have a decision yet, and I’ll share an update once the calls are done.

Eli: The volunteer orientation is still on Wednesday at 7:00 in the community room. We have eight people registered, and I’ve printed the handling guide and the emergency contact sheet.

Tess: I’ll bring the sign-in clipboard and a few spare pens. The room has chairs for 12, but we need to leave the hallway clear because another group meets there at 8:30.

Andre: The donation total from the weekend table was $286.40. I entered it in the monthly ledger and saved the receipt from the card reader with the other March records.

Luis: We also got a bag of unopened treats and two new water bowls. I checked the labels on the treats; they’re sealed and within date, so I added them to the supplies shelf.
